testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What is removed when an air tank is drained?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. These materials can damage the brakes if they build up in the system.

questions.question: When a construction worker is close to the road, you should:

options.text: Wait to proceed until the construction is complete.

questions.explanation: In construction zones, follow the posted speed limit. Slow down more when workers are near the road.

questions.question: What is the maximum fine for driving a CMV without a CDL?
questions.explanation: You can be fined between $75 and $300 for driving a commercial vehicle without the proper license.

questions.question: Distracted drivers may be:

options.text: Preoccupied with using their cell phones.
Not talking to anyone else in their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Preoccupied with using their cell phones.
questions.explanation: You can tell another driver is distracted if they drift between lanes, travel at uneven speeds, use a cell phone or look at a map, or talk to passengers.

questions.question: When conducting a vehicle inspection, you will need to identify all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection, you must check the power steering belt, water pump belt, alternator belt, and air compressor belt for damage or looseness. If any of these parts are not belt-driven, tell the examiner and verify they work properly and are not damaged or leaking.

questions.question: A vehicle equipped with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) can be identified by:

options.text: A sticker on the control panel.
A yellow lamp on the instrument panel.
The letters "ABS" on the brake pedal.
A metal plate on the inside of the driver's side door.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow lamp on the instrument panel.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) if it has a yellow ABS warning light on the instrument panel.

questions.question: While operating a CMV:

options.text: You are not required to wear a safety belt.
You are only required to wear a safety belt if your vehicle does not have airbags.
You are required to wear a safety belt, but only if hauling more than 1,000 pounds of cargo.
You are always required to wear a safety belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are always required to wear a safety belt.
questions.explanation: A safety belt is your best protection in a crash. You must always wear a safety belt while operating a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: While driving, you should:

options.text: Develop plans to get out of any dangerous situation that could arise.
Focus on your own driving and not worry about other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Develop plans to get out of any dangerous situation that could arise.
questions.explanation: While driving, check the road ahead for hazards. Think ahead about how you would handle any problems that might happen.

questions.question: The most common type of foundation brake used is the:
questions.explanation: The S-cam drum brake is the most common type of foundation brake.

questions.question: Regarding winter driving, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Front tires should have a tread depth of at least 4/32 an inch.
Rear tires should have a tread depth of at least 2/32 an inch.
Use a gauge to verify that each tire has a safe tread depth.

questions.explanation: In winter, your tires need good tread to grip the road. Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread, and rear tires need at least 2/32 inch. Use a gauge to check the tread depth.

questions.question: Engine belts should be:
questions.explanation: Check your engine belts for tightness and wear. The right amount of tightness varies by vehicle, so check your owner's manual for your vehicle's requirements.

questions.question: For a single vehicle with air brakes, the maximum air leakage in one minute is ____ psi.
questions.explanation: Air should not leak faster than 2 psi per minute in a static leakage test. If leakage is faster, do not drive the vehicle. Something needs to be repaired.

questions.question: If a truck's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops working:

options.text: The truck will have no brakes.
The truck should only be driven slowly.
The truck will still have brakes.
The truck will have no brakes on the left side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: If the ABS system fails, the truck still has normal brakes. Drive and brake the same way you normally would.

questions.question: After changing a tire, stop after a short distance to:

options.text: Check that the wheel nuts are tight.
Check the air pressure in the tire.
Verify that the correct tire was changed.
Make sure changing the tire did not damage another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the wheel nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop soon to re-check that the wheel nuts are tight.

questions.question: A driver should always:
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead for hazards. Plan what you will do if those hazards become dangerous.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, which is an example of poor lane usage?

options.text: Not driving over curbs or sidewalks
Staying in the leftmost lane when more lanes are available
Finishing a right turn in the rightmost lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Staying in the leftmost lane when more lanes are available
questions.explanation: Do not hit curbs or sidewalks. Stop behind stop lines, crosswalks, and stop signs. Turn in the correct lane. When multiple lanes are available, stay in or move to the rightmost lane.

questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver involved in a crash ahead, you should:

options.text: Block the driver in with your vehicle.
Stop safely and report the aggressive behavior to police.
Pull over and yell at the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely and report the aggressive behavior to police.
questions.explanation: Stop at a safe distance from the crash. Wait for police and tell them about the aggressive driving you saw.

questions.question: To avoid fatigue while driving, take a break every ____:
questions.explanation: On long trips, stop for a break at least every 2 hours or every 100 miles to stay fresh and alert.

questions.question: When backing up, it is best to:

options.text: Use only the passenger's side mirror.
Turn toward the passenger's side when possible.

questions.explanation: Back up slowly and use both side mirrors. Use a helper to watch for obstacles in your blind spots. Agree on a stop signal with your helper.

questions.question: In an engine fire, you should NOT:

options.text: Turn the engine off right away.
Spray foam from under the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Turn off the engine right away. Do not open the hood. Spray foam through the grille or from underneath the vehicle.

questions.question: If a heavy load is slowing you down, you should:

options.text: Keep the vehicle in second gear.

questions.explanation: The right lane is for slower vehicles. If your load is slowing you down, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: If hydraulic brakes fail, you can slow down by:

options.text: Letting the truck run out of gas.

questions.explanation: If your hydraulic brakes fail, shift into a lower gear to help slow your vehicle down.

questions.question: Why should you do the pre-trip inspection steps in the same order each time?

options.text: You will be less likely to forget a step.
The form must be followed in order.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget a step.
questions.explanation: Following the same order each time helps you learn the steps. A routine makes it less likely you will skip or forget a step.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure gets too low in an air brake system?

options.text: The brakes will be very sensitive.

questions.explanation: If air pressure in an air brake system gets too low, the brakes will stop working.

questions.question: When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds how many feet to your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance has four parts: perception, reaction, brake lag, and braking. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: Leaking shock absorbers:

options.text: Will prevent the turn signals from working.
Pose no threat if the vehicle is only driven on highways.

questions.explanation: The suspension system holds the axles in place. Damaged parts like leaking shock absorbers are dangerous defects.

questions.question: What is another name for front-end header boards?
questions.explanation: Front-end header boards are also called "headache racks." They protect the driver if cargo shifts during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: When checking power steering fluid during inspection, which is NOT required?

options.text: Show where the power steering fluid dipstick is located.
Check for adequate power steering fluid.
Ensure that the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
Ensure that the power steering level is above the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ensure that the power steering fluid level is above the full mark.
questions.explanation: You must locate the dipstick and check that the fluid level is adequate and above the refill mark. The fluid does not need to be above the full mark.

questions.question: When visibility is low like at dawn or dusk, you should help other drivers by:

options.text: Waving an arm out the window.

questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights when visibility is low. If you cannot see others, they cannot see you either.

questions.question: During the pre-trip vehicle inspection test:

options.text: Applicants will not have to identify the ABS.
Windshield wipers are not to be addressed.
Shock absorbers only need to be checked on one axle.
The steering box should be checked for leaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering box should be checked for leaks.
questions.explanation: During the external inspection, you must check that the steering box is securely mounted and not leaking.

questions.question: What is a good way to reduce stress while driving?
questions.explanation: Stress while driving can lead to dangerous and aggressive behavior. Listening to calming music can help you relax and stay safe.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off within a few seconds
Stay on until you turn them off manually

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off within a few seconds
questions.explanation: After you start the engine, warning lights and buzzers for oil, coolant, charging systems, and anti-lock brakes should turn off right away.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, if one system has a leak:

options.text: Both systems will always have leaks
The other system may not be affected
The other system will also be affected

questions.correctAnswerText: The other system may not be affected
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate brake systems. A leak in one system may not affect the other system.

questions.question: What is the best way to avoid getting drowsy on a long trip?

options.text: Sleep for only about three hours before the trip
Plan ahead and include stops along the way

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan ahead and include stops along the way
questions.explanation: To prevent drowsy driving, get seven to eight hours of sleep before the trip, drive during hours when you are normally awake, plan breaks during the trip, and exercise regularly.

questions.question: Which of the following is not acceptable emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or six fuses or three liquid burning flares, and a fire extinguisher that is properly charged and rated.

questions.question: If you realize you may be late to your destination, what should you do?

options.text: Use flashing lights to make other drivers move out of your way
Drive at a safe speed and accept when you will arrive

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a safe speed and accept when you will arrive
questions.explanation: To avoid dangerous driving, stay calm and accept delays. Plan for extra time when you are scheduling your trip to help reduce stress about arriving late.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a driving distraction?
questions.explanation: Distractions are activities that take your attention away from driving. This includes eating, drinking, smoking, or adjusting the radio and climate controls. Checking mirrors is a safe driving practice.

questions.question: Where must the ABS malfunction lamp be located on a dolly?
questions.explanation: A dolly with an anti-lock braking system must have a yellow malfunction lamp on its left side.

questions.question: What are placards?

options.text: Warning signs on a vehicle that identify hazardous cargo
A type of tire for snowy conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning signs on a vehicle that identify hazardous cargo
questions.explanation: Placards are diamond-shaped warning signs placed on the outside of vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They identify the specific type of hazard in the cargo.

questions.question: How do states verify that a CDL or CLP driver has only one license?

options.text: By making phone calls to other states
By using a computerized system that connects all states
By looking through the driver's wallet

questions.correctAnswerText: By using a computerized system that connects all states
questions.explanation: All states share CDL and CLP license information in a shared computerized database. When you apply for a license, the state checks this database to make sure you do not already have a license in another state.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread depth of 2/32 of an inch

questions.explanation: Check your tire tread depth. Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch in every groove. Other tires need at least 2/32 of an inch. Tires should not be worn, cracked, or underinflated. All tires should be the same size. Tires from different makers are acceptable.

questions.question: If a tire rim is damaged, what should you do?

options.text: Weld it to repair the damage.
Move it to the axle farthest from the driver.

questions.explanation: Welded wheels or rims are not safe. Replace damaged rims.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test, how are pull-ups treated?

options.text: Points are taken away for each pull-up.
You are allowed three pull-ups per maneuver.
You get points for a pull-up only if you get out of the vehicle first.
Only too many pull-ups count as errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only too many pull-ups count as errors.
questions.explanation: During the basic vehicle control skills test, one pull-up does not result in a penalty. However, too many pull-ups will count as errors.

questions.question: When asked to change lanes during the skills test, what should you do?

options.text: Cut off other vehicles if needed to follow the instructions.
Do not make the lane change if you do not want to.

questions.explanation: You will make several lane changes during the driving skills test. Always check traffic first and use your signals. Change lanes smoothly and safely.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, what should you do?

options.text: Use your brakes the entire way down.
Shift into a higher gear to slow down.
Shift into a lower gear to slow down.
Put the truck in neutral to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a lower gear to slow down.
questions.explanation: When going down a steep hill, use the engine's braking power to slow down. Use your brakes only when needed to prevent them from overheating.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Makes a loud squeaking noise when used.
Helps you stay in control while braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you stay in control while braking.
questions.explanation: ABS gives you better control when braking. It does not necessarily reduce the distance needed to stop.

questions.question: If federal inspectors find your vehicle unsafe, what can they do?

options.text: Take you to a garage to fix your vehicle.
Formally request that you fix your vehicle's problems.
Prevent you from using the vehicle until it is fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent you from using the vehicle until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: Federal or state inspectors can remove an unsafe vehicle from service until it is fixed.

questions.question: What was the purpose of front brake limiting valves?

options.text: Stop the front tires from skidding.
Stop the front tires from overheating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the front tires from skidding.
questions.explanation: Some older air brake vehicles have front brake limiting valves designed to prevent front wheel skidding. However, research shows these devices are not necessary, so they should be left in the normal position.

questions.question: When should placards be used?

options.text: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
If there is empty space in the truck.
If the hazardous materials weigh more than 200 pounds.
If the hazardous materials can be inhaled.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on the outside of vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They show the type of material being carried and warn others of any hazards.

questions.question: What is true about Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS)?

options.text: They work with your normal brakes and do not reduce braking power.
They do not work on large vehicles.
They are illegal in some states.

questions.correctAnswerText: They work with your normal brakes and do not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works alongside your normal braking system. It does not increase or decrease your braking power. ABS activates during hard braking to prevent wheel lockup.
